This snippet will set a picture as your subverse name. Just add it to the bottom of your CSS and change the subverse to your subverse, and add the url to your picture. This needs to be smaller than 50px in height (doesn't have to be, just play around with it). You may or may not have to change the #header-container width, height, etc.... to make this fit correctly.

/* Sub name as image */
/* This makes sure the subverse name text is hidden */
.pagename a[href$="/v/simplegoats"] { /* change this to the name of your subverse but leave the v */
 font-size: 0 !important;
}
/* Set the actual picture to show up */
.pagename a[href$="/v/simplegoats"]:after { /* change this to the name of your subverse but leave the v */
 content: url('Your picture url here'); /* Subverse name or picture url here */
 /* or */
 /* content: "Your text here"; */
 vertical-align: bottom;
}

Year is 1890. Setting is American Southwest. Dragon is Traditional Western fantasy Dragon.
300 Cowboys. They can lasso the fucker to the ground. Plus, I don't think that they're so dumb that they can't shoot the eyeballs.

It depends on how much the dragon's scales could withstand.

The weapons available to the cowboys based on the time Skarnton specified is basically anything they had access to before the Spanish American War. Here is a good link to see what weapons they would have. Only pay attention to the weapons that came out prior to 1890 and that have the American Flag next to them as I doubt they'd be carrying foreign weapons.

Based on what I could see the Cowboys would have revolvers and muskets. As far as revolvers go most of them would probably be Colt .45's. This was pretty much the definitive sidearm of the American West. There are dozens of others, but this one is the most famous, and probably the most effective.
As for muskets, they did not have any automatic rifles yet at this time. Most would probably have a muzzle loader, but there were some breach loaded rifles during this time. Either way, they were single shot weapons.

I honestly think the Dragon could survive all 300 Cowboys shooting it at once. If any did penetrate, they wouldn't be able to go very deep at all. The only real vulnerability would be it's wings.

This is how I see the fight going. The Dragon takes flight and does some strafing runs breathing fire. This may very well take out a third of the cowboys, but we'll say it only takes out a quarter for the sake of the argument. Next the Cowboys to enough damage to the wings to bring it down to earth. They rally at this victory and rush the beast shooting and trying to rope it down. As they charge, the Dragon breathes more fire taking out whoever was dumb enough to approach the head. The ones who came at the sides lasso the spines on it's back or perhaps around the neck or tail but that's less likely. Even if the Cowboys are on horseback, the Dragon shouldn't have little problem lashing it's tail around to send them flying.
At this point the Dragon is probably pretty hurt, but that only makes it more dangerous. The Cowboys are probably down to only a hundred or so left. This could work to their advantage if they spread out and coordinate. The Dragon is probably much faster on the ground than they realize, even with it's large size. It lunges and strikes, taking out several of them each time.

In the end I give this fight to the Dragon 7-8/10. The Cowboys have a small change to win, but only if they are very well coordinated and know exactly where to strike. They would probably have to have some of the act decoy and be sacrificed early on in order to use their numbers to subdue the Dragon. Once they get to depleted they don't stand too much of a chance.

Good In-depth Analysis. I do think that the Dragon has the advantage in this scenario. Cowboys really only have a fighting chance if they are the ones attacking, or if they have a defensive position and they know the dragon is coming. However, I think that If this battle took place 5-10 years later, new weaponry would make a huge difference. I Bet a Gatling gun could do some serious damage to a dragon's wings. The only reason I said 1890 was that I didn't want to get too far away from the true "old west" period.

If the Cowboys are able to bring the dragon to the ground, I think that blinding it would be a major advantage. even if 100 cowboys survived the Dragon's aerial attacks, if most of the remaining firepower was directed to the head, they could disable the dragon and continue to lay down fire from a distance, or get in close and pin the dragon down.

It really depends on the organization and morale of the cowboys.

If the dragon catches them by surprise, i'd say it would be a 95% win ratio for the Dragon. If he cowboys are prepared and have a plan, The dragon' s win ratio would probably drop to 65%

Depends, but I don't think many of the cowboys will have a weapon that can pierce Dragon scale. Still, 300 is a looot of cowboys. The Cowboys can probably win by just sheer attrition and giving the dragon a death by a thousand cuts.
